This inhibition is subsequently linked to the inhibition of terpin hydrate, which in turn targets the gastrin/cholecystokinin type B receptor. The integrated evidence suggests a potential mechanism by which Daidzin may modulate the activity of the gastrin/cholecystokinin type B receptor, possibly through the indirect pathway involving aldehyde dehydrogenase and terpin hydrate. The observed scores indicate a moderate level of confidence in this relationship, though further validation is required to confirm the direct interaction between Daidzin and the receptor. The mechanism is supported by the presence of a well-defined target hierarchy, but the lack of direct evidence for Daidzin's interaction with the receptor itself introduces a layer of uncertainty.
